label: Oreskes
detail: None of the 928 abstracts sampled from 1993–2003 rejected the consensus position.

label: Doran
detail: 97.4% of the actively publishing climate scientists surveyed say human activity is a significant factor — against 82% across all 3146 Earth scientists who responded.

label: Anderegg
detail: 97–98% of the most actively publishing climate researchers support the IPCC's attribution of warming to humans.

label: Cook
detail: Of the 11944 abstracts examined a third stated a position on human-caused warming — and 97.1% of those endorsed it.

label: Verheggen
detail: 91% of the respondents with more than 10 climate publications attribute most warming to greenhouse gases — against 85% across all who stated a position.

label: Stenhouse
detail: 93% of the American Meteorological Society members actively publishing climate research say warming is largely human-caused — against 73% across all members surveyed.

label: Carlton
detail: 96.7% of the surveyed biophysical scientists whose research is mostly on climate agree — against 91.9% across all 698 respondents.

label: Cook
detail: Consensus on consensus — a synthesis of the seven studies above. Agreement spans 90–100% and converges on 97% among the scientists with the most climate expertise.

label: Myers
detail: 98.7% of the confirmed climate experts agree — against 91.1% across all 2548 Earth scientists surveyed in this repeat of Doran & Zimmerman.

label: Lynas
detail: Only 4 of the 3000 papers sampled from 88125 climate papers published since 2012 were skeptical of human-caused warming.
